summary:
Ghost Rovers is an interactive web experience that introduces school-age explorers to NASA's retired space hardware through the story of Sojourner, the first rover on Mars.

Across five chapters, visitors drive the rover, investigate rocks, experience communication delays, and discover why the mission still matters. An explorable 3D model connects the rover's components to their purpose, while a field notebook visualizes NASA's published preliminary APXS measurements of Barnacle Bill, Yogi, and Martian soil. Visitors compare chemical elements and learn how dust can complicate scientific interpretation.

The experience includes desktop and mobile controls, shortcuts for visitors who prefer exploring without driving, and an optional Cardboard-style stereo viewer. Linked NASA sources distinguish documented history from illustrative reconstruction.

By connecting engineering, scientific evidence, and storytelling, Ghost Rovers shows how a silent machine can continue to inspire curiosity. Its mission ended, but the knowledge and engineering lessons it helped establish continue to shape exploration.
details:
GHOST ROVERS is an interactive web experience that brings the story of NASA’s retired space equipment to life. Our first playable story focuses on Sojourner, the Mars Pathfinder rover. Visitors explore its engineering, follow key moments of its mission, and discover why its scientific legacy still matters after its signal has gone silent.

The experience combines five story chapters with hands-on exploration. Visitors guide the rover across an illustrative Martian landscape, approach Barnacle Bill and Yogi, perform simulated instrument scans, and explore the challenges of sunlight, dust, and communication delays. Direct scene-jump controls let visitors follow the story without completing every driving task. A separate engineering view presents eight rover systems, with selectable components, an exploded view, dimensions, and different display modes.

A central feature is the APXS field notebook. Simulated scans reveal published NASA measurements rather than invented scientific results. Visitors compare silicon, magnesium, and iron readings from rock surfaces and windblown soil. The experience also explains how adhering dust affects interpretation, encouraging users to question what measurements can—and cannot—tell us. Links to the original NASA sources are available inside the project.

GHOST ROVERS runs in compatible desktop and mobile browsers without an installation or account. An optional Google Cardboard–style mode provides a stereoscopic view with adjustable eye separation, field of view, and approximate lens correction. Supported phones can use orientation sensors to look around, while dragging provides a fallback. Physical headset comfort and sensor behaviour still require device testing; the main experience works without a headset.

The project is intended for students, educators, and curious visitors. Its creative approach connects emotional storytelling, interactive engineering, and real scientific evidence within one experience. We want people to understand retired hardware through the questions it helped humanity answer, while encouraging curiosity about robotics, planetary exploration, and scientific reasoning.

We developed the prototype using HTML, CSS, JavaScript, Three.js, and WebGL, with procedural 3D models and browser-based interaction. The public website is hosted on Vercel. AI assistance supported code development and explanatory text. During development, we considered mobile usability, rendering performance, clear controls, source attribution, and the distinction between documented history and creative reconstruction. Terrain, routes, timing, and power behaviour are simplified, and the final scene does not claim to depict observed activity after contact was lost.

Explore the project: https://ghostrovers.vercel.app/
